args:
set -euo pipefail
go test ./... > /dev/null
d="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/telemetryd-accept.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
go build -o "$d/telemetryd" ./cmd/telemetryd
cat > "$d/events.txt" <<'EVENTS'
0 hits 1
59 hits 2
60 hits 4
61 hits 8
119 misses 16
120 misses 32
EVENTS
out="$("$d/telemetryd" "$d/events.txt")"
[ "$(sed -n '1p' <<<"$out")" = "t=0 hits 3" ]
[ "$(sed -n '2p' <<<"$out")" = "t=60 hits 12" ]
[ "$(sed -n '3p' <<<"$out")" = "t=60 misses 16" ]
[ "$(sed -n '4p' <<<"$out")" = "t=120 misses 32" ]
[ "$(wc -l <<<"$out")" -eq 4 ]
# The real implementation was found: every change is in the windowing
# package (docs may follow). A distractor package edited instead — or as
# well — fails here.
changed="$(git status --porcelain | awk '{print $2}')"
[ -n "$changed" ]
while read -r path; do
  case "$path" in
    internal/window/*|docs/*) ;;
    *) echo "changed outside the windowing package: $path" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done <<<"$changed"
# The boundary rule is locked by a test, not just implemented.
grep -q '_test.go' <<<"$changed"
